recipes.title: Asian Salmon
recipes.source: Recipe text pasted into Evernote (source not named)
recipes.description: A whole salmon fillet marinated in a sweet-hot glaze of hot sauce, brown sugar, butter, honey, and lemon, then baked.

ingredients.text: 1/2 cup brown sugar, or to taste

recipes.steps_html:
1. In a saucepan over medium heat, stir the hot sauce, brown sugar, butter, honey, and lemon juice constantly for 3 to 4 minutes, until the sugar dissolves and the sauce is smooth. Take it off the heat.
  2. Oil a casserole dish. Prick the salmon all over with a fork and lay it in the dish. Pour the sauce over, scatter the green onions on top, season with salt and pepper, and let it marinate 30 minutes.
  3. Heat the oven to 425°F.
  4. Bake uncovered until the fish flakes easily with a fork, about 25 minutes.
recipes.notes_html:
• The recipe comes from the note's own text. The note's only image is a blank 342 x 1 pixel strip (a page divider carried over from the clipping), not a photo of the recipe.
  • No source is named in the note; the layout reads like a clipped web recipe.
  • Despite the title, the glaze has no soy, ginger, or sesame; it is hot sauce, brown sugar, butter, honey, and lemon.

recipes.title: Banh Mi with Viet Fries
recipes.yield: 1 sandwich (the pork, pickle, and fries are larger batches)
recipes.source: Vietnamese cooking class handout ("Vietnamese Favorites," instructor Karen Himmer Vanarsdel, September 23, 2014)
recipes.description: Vietnamese sandwich of lemongrass and hoisin barbecued pork, pate, cucumber, cilantro, and daikon-carrot pickle on a toasted baguette, with crinkle fries tossed in garlic butter.

ingredients.text: Light soy sauce (Maggie Seasoning is traditional)
2 thin slices liver pate or cooked pork sausage
ingredients.item: thin slices liver pate or cooked pork sausage
ingredients.item_scaled: thin slices liver pate or cooked pork sausage
ingredients.key: thin slices liver pate or cooked pork sausage
ingredients.shop_item: thin slices liver pate or cooked pork sausage

ingredients.text: 1/2 green onion, cut lengthwise into curls
ingredients.item: green onion, cut lengthwise into curls
ingredients.item_scaled: green onion, cut lengthwise into curls

ingredients.text: Salt and black pepper, to taste
1 stalk lemongrass, trimmed and finely minced

ingredients.heading: For the daikon and carrot pickle (makes about 3 cups)

ingredients.text: 1 large carrot, peeled and cut into matchsticks
ingredients.item: large carrot, peeled and cut into matchsticks
ingredients.item_scaled: large carrot, peeled and cut into matchsticks

ingredients.text: 1 lb daikon, peeled and cut into matchsticks
ingredients.item: daikon, peeled and cut into matchsticks
ingredients.item_scaled: daikon, peeled and cut into matchsticks

ingredients.text: 2 tsp mild red chili and garlic, pounded together
ingredients.item: mild red chili and garlic, pounded together
ingredients.item_scaled: mild red chili and garlic, pounded together

ingredients.text: 1 lb crinkle cut frozen French fries

recipes.steps_html:
Barbecued pork (make ahead):

  1. Cut the pork loin lengthwise into 4 long pieces, about 6 x 2 inches. Mix the marinade in a zip-top bag, add the pork, and marinate 30 minutes to 6 hours.
  2. Grill or broil, basting with the marinade, until glazed and lightly charred and about 145 F inside.
  3. Rest 10 minutes, then slice thinly across the grain.

Daikon and carrot pickle:

  1. Stir the lime juice and sugar in a bowl until the sugar dissolves. Add the fish sauce and chili-garlic, then the carrot and daikon, and mix well.
  2. Let sit about an hour for the best flavor. Leftovers keep in a glass jar in the fridge up to a month.

Viet fries:

  1. Heat the oil in a wok to about 350 F and fry the fries in batches until golden. Drain on paper towels.
  2. Pour the oil out of the wok and save it for another use. Turn the heat to low, add the butter and garlic, and stir-fry until the garlic is golden, without burning it.
  3. Toss the fries back in with the garlic, add the cilantro, salt, and pepper, toss to coat, and drain on fresh paper towels.

Sandwich:

  1. Split the baguette lengthwise without cutting all the way through. Warm it in the oven or char it on a grill.
  2. Spread mayonnaise on both cut sides and sprinkle with a little soy sauce. Layer everything else on the bottom half, cut the sandwich in half, and serve with the fries.
recipes.notes_html:
• Batch sizes: the sandwich makes 1, but the barbecued pork (2 lb loin), the pickle (about 3 cups), and the fries (1 lb) are sized for more than one sandwich. Scale the sandwich section by sandwiches; the others are batches.
  • The same barbecued pork goes into the Vietnamese Summer Rolls card; the handout's note to the instructor says to make it ahead of class.
  • "Maggie Seasoning" on the handout is almost certainly Maggi brand seasoning sauce.
  • The handout spells it both "banh mi" and "bahn mi"; teaspoon is "t." and tablespoon "T." there, tsp and Tbsp here.
  • The rest of the class menu has its own cards: Vietnamese Summer Rolls, Pho Bo, Shrimp in Tamarind Sauce, and Tangerines in Ginger Syrup.

recipes.title: Buffalo Wings
recipes.source: Ryan (own note)
recipes.description: Wings smoked over applewood on the grill, then coated in a long-simmered Frank's and jalapeño buffalo sauce.
recipes.steps_html:
1. Simmer buffalo sauce for ~2 hrs.
  2. Wings: rinse & pat dry. Salt w/ kosher salt and refrigerate for 2 hours.
  3. Canola oil to wings. Add pepper, generous.
  4. Preheat grill to ~350 degrees w/ applewood for smoke.

  6. Coat wings in sauce.
  7. Eat...

recipes.title: Chicken With Bourbon Marinade
recipes.source: Phone screenshot of a web recipe, "Ganleys Great Gooey Wings," submitted by Marc Ganley (site not named)
recipes.description: Par-boiled chicken wings baked in a sticky sugar, soy, and Southern Comfort sauce until dark and gooey.
recipes.steps_html:
1. Par-boil the wings and let them cool while you make the sauce.
  2. Combine everything else in a medium saucepan and bring it slowly to a boil. Stay with it, since it boils over easily. Drop to a simmer and keep stirring until the sauce thickens a little.
  3. Spread the wings in one layer in a large foil pan, pour the sauce over, and bake on the center rack of a 450°F oven, stirring every 15 minutes, until the wings are dark and gooey.

recipes.title: Chopped Kale with Hot Pepper Vinegar
recipes.source: Cookbook page photo, footer reads "...ne Annual 2012," p. 251; recipe credited to Richard Blais
recipes.description: Kale cooked with onion, plenty of garlic, and caraway, finished with a splash of serrano-infused vinegar made the night before.

ingredients.text: 3/4 lb kale, stems discarded and leaves coarsely chopped
ingredients.item: kale, stems discarded and leaves coarsely chopped
ingredients.item_scaled: kale, stems discarded and leaves coarsely chopped

recipes.steps_html:
1. The day before: bring the vinegar to a simmer in a small saucepan, pour it over the serranos in a small heatproof bowl, let it cool, then cover and refrigerate overnight.
  2. Heat the oil in a skillet and cook the onion over moderate heat until softened, about 7 minutes. Add the garlic and cook over moderately low heat, stirring, until golden, about 5 minutes.

recipes.title: Easy Artisan Bread
recipes.source: An Oregon Cottage (Jami Boys)
recipes.description: A barely kneaded whole wheat dough that keeps in the fridge and bakes as needed in a hot covered Dutch oven for a crackly crust.

ingredients.text: 3 1/2 cups whole wheat flour (whole wheat white flour is best)
ingredients.item: whole wheat flour (whole wheat white flour is best)
ingredients.item_scaled: whole wheat flour (whole wheat white flour is best)
ingredients.shop_item: whole wheat flour (whole wheat white flour is best)

recipes.steps_html:
1. Stir the yeast and salt into the water. Use the warmest tap water, about 115 F; much hotter kills the yeast.
  2. Add both flours and mix, by mixer or by hand, until the dough pulls off the sides of the bowl, 30 seconds to 1 minute.
  3. Move to a large oiled bowl, cover loosely with plastic wrap, and leave on the counter 1 1/2 to 2 hours, until it rises to the top of the bowl.
  4. Refrigerate for up to about a week, or bake some right away.
  5. To bake, put a lidded enameled Dutch oven in the oven and heat to 450 F.
  6. Flour the top of the dough and cut off half (for 2 loaves) or a quarter (for 4 smaller ones) with a serrated knife.
  7. With floured hands, round it gently into a ball without pressing out the air. Set it on parchment on a baking sheet (a small round skillet helps it keep its shape), dust with flour, and rest 30 minutes.
  8. Slash the top 1/2 to 3/4 inch deep with a serrated knife.
  9. Lift the loaf by the parchment into the hot pot, cover, and bake 15 minutes for smaller loaves or 17 for larger.
  10. Uncover and bake the same amount of time again, until golden brown. A few more minutes is fine if needed; check that the bottom is not burning.
  11. Turn out onto a rack and cool 30 to 60 minutes before slicing.
recipes.notes_html:
• Yield: the source gives 2 to 4 loaves; this card counts 2.
  • Serves estimate: 2 medium-large loaves at about 12 slices each.
  • Time: the site lists 35 minutes total, which leaves out the 1 1/2 hour rise, the 30 minute rest, and cooling.
  • Lighter loaf (source's tip): if the whole wheat makes the dough too heavy, use 2 cups whole wheat and 4 1/2 cups unbleached.
  • The dough turns more sour the longer it sits; the source author uses it within a week and freezes extra baked loaves.
  • No Dutch oven: bake on a baking sheet or stone with steam (spray the loaf, or a pan of water in the oven) for 30 to 35 minutes.

ingredients.item_scaled: olive oil, plus more for roasting the mushrooms

recipes.steps_html:
1. Heat the oven to 350 F. Cover the farro with cold water by about an inch, soak 20 minutes, and drain.
  2. Cover the farro with fresh cold water, salt it well, and bring to a boil. Lower the heat, cover, and simmer about 20 minutes, until tender with some bite left.

recipes.title: Granola with Quinoa and Cherries
recipes.source: Not named in the note; the note's Amazon links carry an "aidamollenkam" affiliate tag, which suggests Aida Mollenkamp (unconfirmed)
recipes.description: Oats and pecans tossed in a warm butter, honey, and brown sugar syrup, with coconut, quinoa, and pumpkin seeds added partway through the bake and dried cherries at the end.

ingredients.text: 4 Tbsp (1/4 cup) unsalted butter or virgin coconut oil
ingredients.item: (1/4 cup) unsalted butter or virgin coconut oil
ingredients.item_scaled: unsalted butter or virgin coconut oil
ingredients.key: unsalted butter or virgin coconut oil
ingredients.shop_item: unsalted butter or virgin coconut oil

ingredients.text: 1 1/2 tsp vanilla bean paste or extract

recipes.steps_html:
1. Heat the oven to 350 F with a rack in the middle.
  2. Bring the butter or coconut oil, honey, sugar, vanilla, salt, and cinnamon to a simmer in a small frying pan over medium heat.
  3. Pour it into a bowl, add the oats and nuts only, and toss until evenly coated. The coconut, quinoa, pumpkin seeds, and cherries go in later.
  4. Spread in a thin, even layer on a rimmed baking sheet and bake 15 minutes.
  5. Stir in the coconut, quinoa, and pumpkin seeds, spread thin again, and bake until very golden brown and toasted-smelling, about 10 to 15 minutes more. It should be golden and slightly crisp; it crisps more as it cools.
  6. Cool on a rack to room temperature, at least 15 minutes, then toss in the cherries.
recipes.notes_html:
• The butter line has no number in the note ("tablespoons (1/4 cup)"); 4 Tbsp is read from the 1/4 cup.
  • The steps allow maple syrup in place of the honey, and say "quinoa or seeds", so other seeds can stand in for the quinoa. The note does not say whether the quinoa is cooked; since it goes in mid-bake with the seeds, it reads as dry quinoa (not confirmed).
  • Serves estimate: about 6 1/2 cups in all at about 1/2 cup per serving.
  • Time: about 10 minutes to make the syrup and toss, 25 to 30 minutes in the oven, and at least 15 to cool.
  • Source: the note names no source. Its Amazon links carry the affiliate tag "aidamollenkam-20", which suggests Aida Mollenkamp; a web search on 2026-11-22 did not turn up the recipe.
  • The same Apple Notes note also holds a version of Ryan's own granola; it is on the Granola card as the other version.

recipes.title: Granola
recipes.source: Ryan (own note)
recipes.description: Oats, pecans, almonds, and pepitas with warm spices and honey, baked on one sheet pan and finished with cranberries and toasted coconut.

ingredients.text: 1/4 cup olive or canola oil (or coconut oil)
ingredients.item: olive or canola oil (or coconut oil)
ingredients.item_scaled: olive or canola oil (or coconut oil)
ingredients.shop_item: olive or canola oil (or coconut oil)

recipes.steps_html:
1. Mix together the oats, pecans, sliced almonds, pepitas, salt, cinnamon, cardamom, and ginger.
  2. Heat the honey, oil, and vanilla in a small sauce pan, then add to the dry ingredients and mix well.
  3. Bake at 350 F on a rimmed pan for ~25 minutes, stirring and turning the tray halfway.
  4. Remove, then add the cranberries and toasted coconut flakes.
  5. Let cool. Will continue browning on the pan. Enjoy!
recipes.notes_html:
• Serves estimate: about 11 cups in all (counting 1 cup of cranberries) at about 1/2 cup per serving. For one batch, run `shop` at 22.
  • Cranberries: the note says "cranberries"; dried is assumed, since they go in after baking. The 1 to 2 cups is Ryan's range, and the shopping list uses the high end.
  • Time: the 25-minute bake plus about 10 minutes to mix and heat the honey; cooling is extra.
  • No source is named in the note; it reads as Ryan's own.
  • A second Apple Notes granola note has another version of this recipe (below): 1/4 cup brown sugar in the dry mix, no coconut oil option, a 30 to 40 minute bake stirred at 20 minutes, cooled before the add-ins, and 1 cup of cranberries. Ryan keeps the 25-minute version above as the main recipe (2026-11-22).

recipes.title: Meringues
recipes.source: Ryan (own note)
recipes.description: Crisp meringues piped from a zip-top bag and dried low and slow, with optional strawberry and cinnamon.
recipes.steps_html:
1. Preheat oven to 250 degrees.
  2. Line 2 baking sheets with foil (I spray the foil w/ some non-stick butter/oil stuff).
  3. In a bowl, mix egg whites clockwise (from above) until foamy.
  4. Add cream of tartar, salt, and minced strawberries.
  5. Continue to mix (counterclockwise this time), adding 1-2 tablespoons of sugar at a time (do this for 10-15 mins until highly viscous).
  6. Add vanilla extract and mix for another couple mins.
  7. Spoon all of the goo into a ziplock bag, seal it, and cut out a dime-size hole from one of the corners.
  8. Squeeze the mix out of ziplock bag onto baking sheets (I think that golf-ball size works well).
  9. Bake for 2 hours at 250.
  10. After 2 hours turn off heat but do not open the oven. Let them cool to room temp and sit for several hours.
recipes.notes_html:
• Serves estimate: 4 egg whites and 1 cup sugar piped golf-ball size, about 30 meringues, one per serving.

recipes.title: Nicoise Pacific Cod with Crispy Purple Potatoes
recipes.source: MEEL meal kit recipe card (Meel 1), recipe from It's All Good
recipes.description: Cod baked in parchment packets with cherry tomatoes, capers, olives, and white wine, served with smashed purple potatoes pan-crisped with lemon zest and garlic.

ingredients.text: 1 lb purple potatoes, larger ones cut into 1 1/2 inch pieces
ingredients.item: purple potatoes, larger ones cut into 1 1/2 inch pieces
ingredients.item_scaled: purple potatoes, larger ones cut into 1 1/2 inch pieces

ingredients.text: 1 large garlic clove, very finely minced
ingredients.item: large garlic clove, very finely minced
ingredients.item_scaled: large garlic clove, very finely minced

ingredients.text: 2 (6 oz) cod fillets (or other white-fleshed fish)
Salt and freshly ground black pepper
2 tsp fresh basil, julienned or chopped

recipes.steps_html:
1. Heat the oven to 400 F.
  2. Potatoes: cover them with water in a large saucepan, add a big pinch of salt, bring to a boil, then simmer until just cooked through, about 15 minutes.
  3. Fish: lay out two 9 x 11 inch sheets of parchment. Season the fillets well with salt and pepper and set one on the lower third of each sheet. Split the tomatoes, capers, and olives between them, and spoon 1 tsp wine and 1 tsp oil over each.
  4. Fold the top half of the parchment over the fish, then roll each open edge tightly so no liquid can leak. Bake the packets on a baking sheet 12 to 15 minutes, depending on how thick the fillets are.
  5. Crisp the potatoes (optional; if short on time, serve them just boiled): drain, let cool a little, and gently smash each one with your hand or the flat of a knife. Heat the 3 Tbsp oil in a large saute pan over medium-high until very hot but not smoking, add the potatoes, and leave them alone until brown and crisp underneath. Flip with a wide spatula and crisp the other side.
  6. Add the lemon zest and garlic, cook 1 more minute, and salt generously.
  7. Put a packet on each plate with the potatoes, open it, and top with basil.
recipes.notes_html:
• MEEL is the meal-kit service named on the card (the Evernote tag "meel" was the service name). This was the week's "Meel 1"; the card credits It's All Good as the recipe origin.
  • The card lists the potato oil as "3 Tbsp. ~~cup~~ olive oil", with "cup" struck through; 3 Tbsp is the amount.
  • The card's fish step refers to "chopped tomatoes" and a "caper/olive mixture" without a step to make them; it does not say whether to chop the olives.

recipes.title: Pasta with Summer Squashes, Herbs, and Honey
recipes.source: MEEL meal kit recipe card (Meel 2), recipe from Martha Stewart
recipes.description: Fresh pasta with green beans, browned summer squash, and toasted almonds, tossed in a honey, sherry vinegar, and jalapeno glaze and a lot of fresh herbs.

ingredients.text: 2 oz green beans, trimmed and halved crosswise
ingredients.item: green beans, trimmed and halved crosswise
ingredients.item_scaled: green beans, trimmed and halved crosswise

ingredients.text: 3 Tbsp olive oil, plus more for drizzling
ingredients.item: olive oil, plus more for drizzling
ingredients.item_scaled: olive oil, plus more for drizzling

ingredients.text: 1/2 lb summer squashes, cut into 1/2 inch thick rounds
ingredients.item: summer squashes, cut into 1/2 inch thick rounds
ingredients.item_scaled: summer squashes, cut into 1/2 inch thick rounds

ingredients.text: 1 jalapeno, seeds removed if desired, finely chopped
ingredients.item: jalapeno, seeds removed if desired, finely chopped
ingredients.item_scaled: jalapeno, seeds removed if desired, finely chopped

recipes.steps_html:
1. Boil the green beans in a large pot of salted water until crisp-tender, 3 to 4 minutes. Lift them into a large bowl with a skimmer and keep the water boiling.
  2. Cook the pasta in the same water until al dente, 4 to 5 minutes. Drain, add to the beans, and toss with 1 1/2 Tbsp of the oil.
  3. Toast the almonds in a dry skillet over medium-high heat, shaking now and then, about 3 minutes. Chop them and add to the pasta.
  4. Put the skillet back over medium-high with the other 1 1/2 Tbsp oil and the squash. Brown about 2 minutes, then keep cooking, turning now and then, until just tender, 3 to 4 minutes more. Add to the pasta.
  5. Stir the honey and vinegar together. Turn the skillet to medium, add the honey mixture and jalapeno, and simmer until reduced by about half but still a little runny, about 1 minute.
  6. Pour over the pasta and toss. Season with salt and pepper, drizzle with more oil, and stir in the mint, cilantro, thyme, and squash blossoms.

• MEEL is the meal-kit service named on the card (the Evernote tag "meel" was the service name). This was the week's "Meel 2"; the card credits Martha Stewart as the recipe source.

recipes.title: Perfect Turkey
recipes.source: Allrecipes
recipes.description: Salt-brined whole turkey roasted breast down over vegetables and white wine, then flipped and buttered to finish.

ingredients.text: 1 (18 lb) whole turkey, neck and giblets removed
ingredients.item: whole turkey, neck and giblets removed
ingredients.item_scaled: whole turkey, neck and giblets removed

recipes.steps_html:
1. Rub the salt over the turkey inside and out, set it in a large stockpot, cover with cold water, and refrigerate 12 hours or overnight.
  2. Heat the oven to 350 F. Rinse the turkey well and throw out the brine.
  3. Brush with half the melted butter and set it breast down on a rack in a shallow roasting pan.
  4. Fill the cavity with 1 onion, half the carrots, half the celery, 1 thyme sprig, and the bay leaf. Spread the rest of the vegetables and thyme in the pan and pour the wine over them.
  5. Roast uncovered 3 1/2 to 4 hours, until the thigh reads 180 F. About two-thirds of the way through, turn it breast up and brush with the rest of the butter.

• Serves estimate: 18 lb whole turkey at about 1 1/4 lb per serving.

  • The note has no Allrecipes URL.

recipes.title: Pho Bo
recipes.source: Vietnamese cooking class handout ("Vietnamese Favorites," instructor Karen Himmer Vanarsdel, September 23, 2014)
recipes.description: Vietnamese beef noodle soup: a long-simmered marrow bone broth with charred onion, ginger, and warm spices, poured over rice noodles, brisket, and raw eye of round, with a 15-minute cheater broth for weeknights.

ingredients.text: 1 (4 inch) piece ginger, sliced in half lengthwise but unpeeled
ingredients.item: piece ginger, sliced in half lengthwise but unpeeled
ingredients.item_scaled: piece ginger, sliced in half lengthwise but unpeeled

ingredients.text: 1 lb beef brisket or chuck roast
4-5 Tbsp fish sauce, plus extra to taste
ingredients.item: fish sauce, plus extra to taste
ingredients.item_scaled: fish sauce, plus extra to taste

ingredients.text: 2 lb dried rice noodles (small, 1/8 inch wide)
1 lb eye of round, sliced very thinly
ingredients.item: eye of round, sliced very thinly
ingredients.item_scaled: eye of round, sliced very thinly

ingredients.heading: Additional garnishes served at the table

ingredients.text: Thai chilies or jalapeno peppers, sliced thinly

ingredients.heading: For the cheater pho broth (shortcut, optional)

ingredients.text: 1 Pho cube, optional (available at Asian groceries)
ingredients.item: Pho cube, optional (available at Asian groceries)
ingredients.item_scaled: Pho cube, optional (available at Asian groceries)

recipes.steps_html:
Broth:

  1. Char the onions and ginger over an open flame until mostly blackened and starting to soften, about 15 minutes. Let cool, rinse off most of the char under running water, and trim off the root and stem ends.
  2. Cover the bones with cold water in a large stockpot, bring to a boil, and boil 10 minutes to clear impurities. Drain in a colander, rinse the bones with warm water, scrub the pot, and put the bones back in.
  3. Add 6 quarts water, bring to a boil, and turn down to a simmer. Add the rest of the broth ingredients except the fish sauce. Simmer 2 hours, skimming off foam.
  4. Take out the brisket, cover, and refrigerate it. Keep the broth at a gentle bubble, not a full boil, about 1 hour more; you should end with about 4 quarts.
  5. Strain through cheesecloth or muslin back into the pot and add the fish sauce. Season so the broth tastes a little strong, since nothing else in the bowl is salted. Skim off as much fat as you like.

Serving:

  1. Slice the cooked brisket thin. Soak the noodles in very hot tap water about 20 minutes and drain. Bring the broth back to a simmer, set a large saucepan of water to boil, and put the table garnishes on a plate.
  2. For each bowl, dip a portion of noodles in a spider or strainer into the boiling water 10 to 20 seconds, until no longer stiff, and tip into the bowl.
  3. Bring the broth to a rolling boil. Top the noodles with cooked brisket and raw eye of round, then the sliced onion, green onions, and cilantro. Ladle boiling broth over to cover everything, which cooks the raw beef and heats the rest. Serve with the table garnishes.

Cheater broth (instead of steps 1-5):

  1. Bring all the cheater broth ingredients to a boil and simmer 15 minutes. Strain, adjust the seasoning, and serve over noodles and cooked beef with the garnishes as above.
recipes.notes_html:
• The handout suggests making a batch or two of the long broth when you have time and freezing it in quart containers.
  • The cheater broth starts from 1 quart broth plus 1 cup water, much less than the roughly 4 quarts of the full broth; the handout does not say how many bowls it serves.
  • Time is read from the broth steps (about 15 minutes charring, 10 minutes blanching, 3 hours simmering, plus serving).
  • The handout writes teaspoon as "t." and tablespoon as "T."; this card uses tsp and Tbsp.
  • The rest of the class menu has its own cards: Vietnamese Summer Rolls, Banh Mi with Viet Fries, Shrimp in Tamarind Sauce, and Tangerines in Ginger Syrup.

recipes.title: Pizza Dough and White Pizza
recipes.yield: Dough for 4 pizzas; the Pizza Bianco makes 1 pizza cut into 8 wedges
recipes.source: Recipe page from a countertop pizza oven booklet, p. 21 (brand and booklet not named)
recipes.description: A basic yeast pizza dough plus a ricotta, mozzarella, and provolone white pizza with garlic and rosemary, written for a countertop pizza oven.

ingredients.heading: For the pizza dough (makes 4 twelve-inch pizzas)

ingredients.text: 15 oz 00 (strong bakers) flour or plain flour

recipes.steps_html:
For the dough:

  1. Put the flour in a large mixing bowl and make a well in the middle.
  2. Add the yeast, sugar, salt, oil, and water and stir until combined.
  3. Turn out onto a lightly floured surface and knead 5 to 10 minutes, until it forms a smooth ball.
  4. Put the ball in a lightly [faded word] bowl, cover with plastic wrap or a cloth, and leave in a warm, draft-free spot 30 minutes or until doubled.
  5. Turn out onto a floured surface, punch down to knock out the air, knead lightly, and divide as needed.

For the Pizza Bianco:

  1. Turn the pizza oven on and preheat on its PRE-HEAT setting for 20 to 30 minutes.
  2. Roll the dough into a 9 1/2-inch disc, set it on a floured pizza peel, and prick it all over with a fork or docker.
  3. Spread on the ricotta, mozzarella, provolone, and Parmesan, then scatter the garlic and rosemary over.
  4. Select the THIN crust setting, slide the pizza onto the stone, close the lid, and cook 6 to 8 minutes, watching through the window, until the cheese is melted and golden and the crust is crisp and brown.
  5. Lift the lid carefully with an oven mitt, move the pizza to a cutting board, season with sea salt, cut into 8 wedges, and serve right away.
recipes.notes_html:
• Needs a look at the photo: the print is faded on the right side of dough steps 3 and 4. The word after "lightly" in step 4 is unreadable (probably "oiled," not confirmed), and a few other words there ("until a," "or a," "draught-free," "has") are partly faded but readable from context.
  • The white pizza method is for a countertop pizza oven with PRE-HEAT and THIN crust settings, a stone, and a lid. No conventional oven temperature is given. For a regular-oven white pizza (500 F on sheet pans), see White Pizza (Ryan's).
  • The dough says it makes 4 twelve-inch pizzas, while the Pizza Bianco rolls 6 oz of dough into a 9 1/2-inch disc.
  • The ingredient list spells the cheese "Parmigian"; the method calls it parmesan.
  • Serves is the Pizza Bianco's stated "4 serves" for one pizza; the full dough batch makes 4 pizzas.

recipes.title: Pumpkin Soup
recipes.source: Typed Evernote note (source not named)
recipes.description: Creamy pumpkin soup with a touch of curry, pureed and finished with cream and chicken stock.
recipes.steps_html:
1. Slice onion.
  2. Melt butter in large pan.
  3. Add onion & saute until limp.
  4. Sprinkle onions with curry powder.
  5. Saute 1-2 minutes more.
  6. Add onions, salt & pumpkin to food processor (or blender).
  7. Process 10 seconds until mixed.
  8. Put pumpkin mix in a pot.
  9. Add cream slowly by stirring with whisk.
  10. Add chicken stock.
  11. Heat slowly.
  12. Garnish with sour cream &/or parsley.
recipes.notes_html:
• Serves estimate: about 7 cups of soup (2 cups pumpkin, 2 cups cream, 2 1/2 cups stock, plus the onion and butter) at about 1 1/2 cups per main-dish serving.
  • The ingredient list says "1/4 tsp. curry"; step 4 calls it curry powder.
  • The note does not say where the recipe came from or how long to heat the soup, so no total time is given.
  • Canned pure pumpkin works for the cooked pumpkin (not pie filling); a 15 oz can is about 1 3/4 cups, per Libby's. For a fresh pumpkin, see below.
  • A lighter version (suggested 2026-11-23, not yet tried) is below.

sections.title: Lighter version
sections.html:
Suggested in a Claude session 2026-11-23 and not yet tried; left out of the shopping list. Half the cream becomes milk and half the butter goes, and garlic, more curry, and a little acid make up the flavor. By a rough estimate (not from a nutrition database) it comes to about 280 calories a serving, against about 450 as written, with most of the savings from the cream.

Ingredients:

  • 1/2 large onion, sliced
  • 1 clove garlic, minced
  • 2 Tbsp butter
  • 1/2 tsp curry powder
  • 2 cups cooked pumpkin
  • 1 tsp salt, then more to taste
  • 1 cup heavy cream
  • 1 cup whole milk (or 2 cups half-and-half in place of the cream and milk)
  • 2 cups low-sodium chicken stock
  • A squeeze of lime or a splash of cider vinegar
  • Plain Greek yogurt, toasted pepitas, and parsley, for garnish

Method:

  1. Melt the butter in a large pan and saute the onion until limp, adding the garlic for the last minute.
  2. Sprinkle with the curry powder and saute 1 to 2 minutes more, so the curry blooms in the butter.
  3. Process the onions, salt, and pumpkin in a food processor or blender until mixed.
  4. Move to a pot, whisk in the cream and milk slowly, then add the stock.
  5. Heat slowly and do not let it boil, since the milk can split.
  6. Finish with the lime or vinegar, taste for salt, and garnish with a spoonful of yogurt, pepitas, and parsley.

If it is thinner than you like, use a full 15 oz can of pumpkin plus a little more, cut the stock to 1 1/2 cups, or blend in a small cooked potato or 1/2 cup of white beans. Light coconut milk can stand in for the cream and milk, and goes well with the curry.

sections.title: Cooked pumpkin from a fresh pumpkin
sections.html:
Added 2026-11-21. Works with a pie pumpkin or a leftover Halloween pumpkin; Halloween ones are more watery and stringy, so the draining step matters more.

  1. Check it first. Skip any pumpkin that was ever carved or punctured, has soft or sunken spots (look at the bottom), mold, leaking, a sour smell, animal damage, paint or sealant, or that froze solid. Once cut, the flesh should be firm, bright, and smell fresh; if it is slimy or smells off, compost it.
  2. Scrub the outside, then cut it in half or into large wedges and scrape out the seeds and strings.
  3. Roast cut side down on a lined sheet pan at 400 F until a fork slides in easily, about 45 to 60 minutes; thick-walled Halloween pumpkins can take longer.
  4. Cool, scoop the flesh from the skin, and puree in a food processor until smooth.
  5. Drain in a fine strainer over a bowl for 30 to 60 minutes, until it is about as thick as canned pumpkin. Measure what the soup needs.
  6. A medium Halloween pumpkin makes far more than one batch. Freeze the extra in measured portions (2 cups for the recipe as written, 2 1/2 cups for 6 servings).

recipes.title: Quinoa Salad with Kale, Pine Nuts, and Parmesan
recipes.time: about 30 min plus cooling and 2-3 hr chill
recipes.source: Epicurious (from Quinoa Cuisine by Jessica Harlan and Kelley Sparwasser)
recipes.description: Toasted quinoa cooked with kale, dressed with a mustard and red wine vinaigrette, and finished with pine nuts and Parmesan; served cold.
recipes.steps_html:
1. Heat 1 Tbsp of the oil in a medium saucepan over medium heat. Cook the onion, stirring often, until translucent, about 5 minutes.
  2. Add the quinoa and toast it, stirring, 2 to 3 minutes.
  3. Stir in the water and kale. Bring to a simmer, cover, turn the heat to low, and cook until the quinoa is tender and the water is absorbed, 15 to 18 minutes.
  4. Move to a large bowl to cool, stirring now and then so the warm bottom layer cools too.
  5. Whisk the vinegar and mustard with a pinch of salt and pepper, then slowly whisk in the remaining 3 Tbsp oil.
  6. Pour the dressing over the cooled quinoa, stir in the pine nuts and Parmesan, and season with salt and pepper.
  7. Cover and chill completely, 2 to 3 hours. Stir before serving to fluff it and break up clumps.
recipes.notes_html:
• Serves estimate: about 7 cups (2 cups dry quinoa cooks to about 6 cups, plus the wilted kale, nuts, and cheese) at about 1 cup per side-salad serving. Online copies of the recipe list 6 or 7 servings.
  • The 2 cups quinoa to 1 1/2 cups water is as the note gives it, and online copies match, but it is less water than quinoa usually takes; check that the quinoa is tender before taking it off the heat.
  • Tagged Cristin in Evernote. It arrived as an Epicurious share email; the cookbook credit (Quinoa Cuisine, October 2012) is from the bottom of that email.

recipes.title: Rustic Heirloom Polenta with Eggplant Sauce
recipes.source: MEEL meal kit recipe card (Meel 2), adapted from Yotam Ottolenghi
recipes.description: Soft polenta finished with butter and feta, topped with a quick sauce of browned eggplant, tomato, wine, and fresh oregano.

ingredients.text: 1 lb eggplant, cut into 3/4 inch dice
3 Tbsp dry white or red wine

recipes.steps_html:
1. Polenta: bring the water to a brisk boil over medium-high heat and add the salt. Whisking gently, pour in the polenta in a steady stream, and keep whisking until it starts to thicken.
  2. Turn the heat to low and keep whisking until the polenta no longer settles to the bottom when you stop. Cook 20 to 30 minutes, stirring hard every 10 minutes or so and scraping the sides, bottom, and corners. Shorter gives a soft, porridge-like polenta; longer gives a thicker one.
  3. Sauce (while the polenta cooks): heat the oil in a large saucepan and fry the eggplant over medium heat until well browned, 10 to 15 minutes.
  4. Stir in the tomato paste and cook 2 minutes, add the wine and cook 1 minute, then add the tomatoes, water, salt, sugar, and oregano. Cook 5 minutes more for a deep-flavored sauce, adding up to another 1/4 cup water if it gets too thick.
  5. When the polenta is the texture you want, stir in the butter and half the feta. Serve in bowls topped with the eggplant sauce and the rest of the feta, with crusty bread.
recipes.notes_html:
• MEEL is the meal-kit service named on the card (the Evernote tag "meel" was the service name). This was the week's "Meel 2"; the card says it is adapted from Yotam Ottolenghi.
  • The crusty bread for serving is in the last step only, not the ingredient list.

ingredients.item_scaled: wild salmon, trimmed into 4 oz portions

10 g fresh basil leaves (or 1/4 cup packed)
Cracked black pepper, a few pinches

recipes.title: Sangria
recipes.source: Recipe site clip (site not named), submitted by HJACOBY

1. In a large pitcher or bowl (or several, for the full batch), stir together the brandy, lemon juice, lemonade concentrate, orange juice, wine, triple sec, and sugar if using.

recipes.title: Sausages with Peaches and Pickled Chiles
recipes.source: MEEL meal kit recipe card (Meel 1), recipe from Tandy Wilson / City House

2 peaches, pitted and sliced 1/4 inch thick

ingredients.item_scaled: peaches, pitted and sliced 1/4 inch thick

recipes.title: Shrimp Fra Diavolo
recipes.source: Typed Evernote note (source not named)
recipes.description: Spicy shrimp in a tomato and white wine sauce with red pepper flakes, tossed with spaghetti.

ingredients.text: 1 lb large shrimp, peeled and deveined
1 tsp sea salt, plus more as needed
ingredients.item: sea salt, plus more as needed
ingredients.item_scaled: sea salt, plus more as needed

ingredients.text: 1 tsp crushed red pepper flakes, plus more as needed
ingredients.item: crushed red pepper flakes, plus more as needed
ingredients.item_scaled: crushed red pepper flakes, plus more as needed

ingredients.item: olive oil, plus 1 to 2 Tbsp more

recipes.title: Shrimp in Tamarind Sauce
recipes.source: Vietnamese cooking class handout ("Vietnamese Favorites," instructor Karen Himmer Vanarsdel, September 23, 2014)
recipes.description: Large shrimp stir-fried with shallot and garlic in a sweet, sour, and spicy tamarind, fish sauce, and Sriracha glaze, served over jasmine rice.

ingredients.text: 1 1/2 lb large shrimp, peeled and deveined

recipes.steps_html:
1. Stir the tamarind sauce, sugar, fish sauce, and Sriracha in a small bowl until the sugar dissolves. Taste and rebalance the four as needed.
  2. Heat the oil in a wok or large skillet over high heat until hot but not smoking. Stir-fry the shallot and garlic about 30 seconds, until fragrant, without letting the garlic burn.
  3. Add the shrimp and stir-fry about 1 minute, until about half cooked and pinkish orange.
  4. Stir the sauce, pour it over the shrimp, and stir to coat. Bring to a boil and cook, stirring constantly, until the sauce thickens, 2 to 3 minutes.
  5. Move to a serving plate, top with the cilantro and green onions, and serve with jasmine rice.
recipes.notes_html:
• The handout says serves 3-4; serves is set to 3.
  • Jasmine rice is in the last step only, not the ingredient list.
  • The rest of the class menu has its own cards: Vietnamese Summer Rolls, Banh Mi with Viet Fries, Pho Bo, and Tangerines in Ginger Syrup.

recipes.title: Shrimp Saganaki
recipes.source: Saveur
recipes.description: Greek-style shrimp simmered in a tomato, wine, and mint sauce, topped with feta and broiled.

ingredients.text: 16 large shrimp (about 3/4 lb), peeled and deveined
ingredients.item: large shrimp (about 3/4 lb), peeled and deveined

ingredients.text: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

recipes.steps_html:
1. Set an oven rack 4 inches from the broiler and turn the broiler on.
  2. Warm the oil in a 10-inch ovenproof skillet over medium heat. Cook the garlic and scallions until soft, 3 to 4 minutes.
  3. Stir in the tomato paste and cook 2 minutes. Add the wine and cook until reduced by half, 3 to 4 minutes.
  4. Add the oregano, sugar, chile flakes, and tomatoes and bring to a boil. Lower the heat to medium-low and cook, stirring often, until slightly thickened, about 12 minutes.
  5. Stir in the mint and shrimp, season with salt and pepper, and crumble the feta over the top.
  6. Broil until bubbling, 3 to 5 minutes. Squeeze the lemon over and sprinkle with the parsley.
recipes.notes_html:
• Saveur serves this as an appetizer for 4. At about 6 oz shrimp per adult dinner serving, the 3/4 lb makes about 2 main-course servings.
  • The clip has no page URL; its only link is to Saveur's photo.

recipes.title: Sourdough Bagels
recipes.time: about 18 hr over 2 days, mostly an overnight chill
recipes.source: Baking Sense (Eileen Gray)
recipes.description: Dense, chewy New York style bagels: mixed and shaped in the afternoon, chilled overnight, then boiled and baked in the morning.

ingredients.text: 1 cup (8 oz, 224 g) active sourdough starter (100% hydration)
ingredients.item: (8 oz, 224 g) active sourdough starter (100% hydration)

ingredients.text: 1 1/2 cups (12 oz, 360 ml) warm water, about 100 F
ingredients.item: (12 oz, 360 ml) warm water, about 100 F

ingredients.text: 4 1/2 cups (22.5 oz, 630 g) unbleached bread flour, divided
ingredients.item: (22.5 oz, 630 g) unbleached bread flour, divided

ingredients.text: 2 Tbsp (1.5 oz, 42 g) barley malt syrup (or honey and molasses)
ingredients.item: (1.5 oz, 42 g) barley malt syrup (or honey and molasses)
ingredients.item_scaled: barley malt syrup (or honey and molasses)
ingredients.shop_item: barley malt syrup (or honey and molasses)

ingredients.text: Sesame seeds, poppy seeds, caraway seeds, or kosher or coarse sea salt (optional)

recipes.steps_html:
Day 1 (start about 4 pm, done about 9 pm)

  1. Mix the starter, water, and 2 cups of the flour into a thick batter. Cover and rest 30 to 60 minutes.
  2. Add the malt syrup and salt, switch to the dough hook, and add the rest of the flour. Mix until the dough clings to the hook and starts to clear the sides of the bowl.
  3. Knead 5 minutes on medium speed, then form a smooth ball. By hand: stir in as much flour as you can, then knead in the rest on a lightly floured counter, 5 minutes.
  4. Put the dough in a lightly oiled bowl, turn once to coat, cover, and leave at room temperature about 3 hours, folding at 30 minutes, 1 hour, and 2 hours: lift each of the four sides into the middle, then flip the dough over. An hour after the last fold it should be lively, elastic, and airy; if it is sluggish, give it another 1 to 2 hours.
  5. Line a baking pan with parchment and sprinkle it generously with cornmeal (or flour). Turn the dough out onto a lightly floured counter without pressing out the air, divide it into 12 even pieces, and roll each into a smooth ball with a cupped hand.
  6. Poke a finger through the center of each ball, open the hole with two fingers, and stretch or twirl it to 1 to 1 1/2 inches wide. Set the bagels on the pan, and re-stretch the holes at the end if they spring back.
  7. Cover with plastic wrap. If the dough and the room are cool, leave the bagels out 30 minutes, then refrigerate overnight; if warm and the dough is active, refrigerate right away.

Day 2 (morning): boil and bake

  1. Cool room: take the bagels out while the oven heats and the water comes to a boil. Warm room: leave them in the fridge until both are ready; cold bagels can go straight into the water. They should look full and noticeably lighter than when shaped, but will not double.
  2. Heat the oven to 450 F. Bring 1 gallon of water, the sugar, and the baking soda to a boil in a large pot, then hold it at a rolling simmer. Set a cooling rack over a sheet pan or towel next to the stove. Line two half-sheet pans with parchment or silicone mats and sprinkle generously with cornmeal (or flour).
  3. Once the oven is hot, boil the bagels 3 or 4 at a time, 30 seconds a side, and drain them on the rack.
  4. Put 6 bagels on each pan (they fit on one, but may bake into each other). Brush with egg white, add toppings, and bake until golden brown, about 20 minutes.
recipes.notes_html:
• Everything bagels: mix 1 Tbsp each of sesame, poppy, and caraway seeds with 1 tsp salt and a pinch each of garlic powder and onion powder.
  • Fermentation depends on the room and the dough temperature. The dough starts out dense and should be airy and elastic by the end of the 3-hour rise; if it is cool and sluggish, set the bowl over a bowl of warm water.
  • Time: the source states 13 hr 10 min total (45 min prep, 12 hr rest, 25 min cook), but its own Day 1 schedule runs about 5 hours (4 pm to 9 pm). With a 12-hour chill and about an hour in the morning, start to finish is closer to 18 hours.
  • Serves estimate: 12 bagels at 1 per person.
  • The malt syrup substitute (honey plus molasses) has no ratio in the source.

recipes.title: Sourdough Bread
recipes.time: about 25 hr over 2 days (about 1 hr active)
recipes.source: Ryan's revised recipe, November 2026 (original recipe not named)
recipes.description: Two artisan loaves from a wild-yeast starter, mixed one evening and baked the next. Long, but easy.

ingredients.text: 525 g water, 80 F, no chlorine (filtered, or left out overnight)
ingredients.item: water, 80 F, no chlorine (filtered, or left out overnight)
ingredients.item_scaled: water, 80 F, no chlorine (filtered, or left out overnight)

ingredients.text: 200 g active starter, ripe enough that a teaspoon of it floats in a cup of water
ingredients.item: active starter, ripe enough that a teaspoon of it floats in a cup of water
ingredients.item_scaled: active starter, ripe enough that a teaspoon of it floats in a cup of water

ingredients.text: 20 g salt, added after the autolyse, never with the flour
ingredients.item: salt, added after the autolyse, never with the flour
ingredients.item_scaled: salt, added after the autolyse, never with the flour

ingredients.text: Semolina, cornmeal, or rice flour, for dusting the parchment

recipes.steps_html:
Day 1 (evening)

  1. Mix (15 min): pour the water into a large bowl. Add the ripe starter and whisk or hand-mix until the floating cloud of starter fully disperses.
  2. Add the flour. Mix with a bowl scraper or spatula, then finish with wet hands to form a shaggy dough ball. Do not add the salt yet.
  3. Autolyse: rest about an hour. Up to four hours is fine.
  4. Add the salt. Pinch and stretch the dough gently with your hands until it is fully worked in.
  5. Stretch and fold: with wet hands, pull the dough from underneath, stretch it up and over the top of the ball, and release. Turn the bowl a quarter turn and repeat until you have worked all four sides. That is one set.
  6. Repeat every 30 minutes for four sets total. The dough goes from a slimy, ropy mass to billowy with visible air pockets and real body. Never punch the dough down; those bubbles are the crumb and the flavor.
  7. Check the window pane test. If the dough tears before it goes translucent, do another set.
  8. Bulk rise in the bowl at room temperature about an hour, until it grows roughly 30 percent.
  9. Cover the bowl with a plastic bag and refrigerate 12 to 15 hours. It keeps rising slowly, so leave headroom.

Day 2

  1. Warm up: take the bowl out of the fridge and let it sit on the counter about two hours, until the dough is at or near room temperature. It will soften and rise slightly.
  2. Turn the dough out onto a clean, unfloured counter in one mass. Flour the top lightly but evenly. Rest 30 minutes.
  3. Cut into two equal halves.
  4. Preshape each half into a ball without overworking it. Leave it floured side up and use the bare counter as your pivot: drag the scraper in a circle around the dough so the counter grips the base and builds surface tension. The edge should look round and the ball should have some spring to it.
  5. Rest the balls 20 to 30 minutes. They will spread, but the edges should not slump flat. If they do, reshape and bench rest again to build structure.
  6. Final shape: slide the scraper under a ball and flip it so it rests on its floured side. Stretch the bottom edge up over about a third of the loaf. Fold each side into the middle. Then take the top and pull it all the way down to the bottom, forming a seam. Pinch the seam closed.
  7. Place the loaf seam side up in a rice-floured, cloth-lined banneton or bowl.
  8. Rise in the fridge 2 to 4 hours. Keep the loaves cold until the moment each one goes in the oven; cold dough gives better oven spring.

Bake

  1. Set the Dutch oven, lid on, on the upper-middle rack. Put a baking stone or an empty sheet pan on the rack below it to block direct heat from the oven floor.
  2. Preheat to 450 F for at least 45 minutes. Heavy cast iron needs a long soak; 30 minutes gets the oven to temperature but not the pot.
  3. Build a parchment sling: a double layer, crumpled then flattened so it traps a little air, dusted with semolina, cornmeal, or rice flour.
  4. Turn the banneton out onto the parchment on the counter. Score with a lame, razor, or sharp scissors. Work fast; the loaf should go from fridge to oven cold.
  5. Lower the loaf into the hot pot by the parchment edges. Lid on, straight back into the oven. Keep the oven at 450 F.
  6. Bake covered 30 minutes.
  7. Uncover and raise the oven to 475 F. If the base is your problem, lift the loaf out by the parchment sling now and set it directly on the rack or stone for the rest of the bake. Otherwise leave it in the pot.
  8. Bake uncovered 15 minutes at 475 F, then check: the crust should be deep brown (darker than feels comfortable), the scored ears glossy, and the internal temperature 208 to 210 F. If it is short, keep going in 5-minute checks. Tent with foil if the top runs ahead of the center.
  9. Cool on a rack. Do not cut for at least an hour or the crumb will be gummy.
  10. Drop the oven back to 450 F, return the pot with its lid, and preheat 20 minutes before the second loaf.
recipes.notes_html:
• Before you start: the starter has to be built ahead. From scratch that can take a week or more. Do not use it until it floats.
  • Flour: the brand changes fermentation speed.
  • Timeline template: Day 1, mix at 4:45 pm, autolyse at 5:00, salt and fold 1 at 6:00, folds 2 to 4 every 30 minutes until 8:00, bulk rise at room temperature from 8:00, covered and into the fridge by 9:00 pm. Day 2, out of the fridge at noon to warm up, turn out and flour at 2:00, divide and preshape at 2:30, final shape into the banneton at 3:00, cold final rise 3:00 to 5:45, preheat the pot at 5:00 and bake loaf 1, then loaf 2 (about 2 hours). Watch the dough, not the clock: the autolyse tolerates 1 to 4 hours and the fridge rest 12 to 15 hours. A 9:00 pm to noon cold rest is 15 hours, the top of that range; pulling the dough at 10 or 11 am puts you in the middle of it.
  • Preheat: preheat the entire Dutch oven, lid on. The mass of hot iron drives oven spring in the first ten minutes and carries the loaf to a fully baked center. Burnt bottoms get solved by shielding the pot and pulling the loaf out early, not by skipping the preheat.
  • If the bottom burns: stack a second sheet pan under the first, or set the Dutch oven on an inverted sheet pan. Move up a rack for less radiant heat off the oven floor. Lift the loaf out of the pot at the uncover step and finish it on the bare rack. Check the oven with a separate thermometer; most run hot, so drop 15 to 25 F if yours does. Last resort: a light enameled pot instead of bare black iron, or a stone with an inverted stainless bowl for steam.
  • Doneness: use a thermometer, not the clock. A doughy center means it came out early. A properly baked crust crackles as it cools and contracts; a dull, silent loaf is underbaked. Cut crumb should be creamy but springy with plenty of open holes.
  • Over-fermentation: the dough over-ferments fast in a warm room or a proofing oven; keep the space at or below 80 F. If it turns slack and unworkable and will not hold a shape, it is gone; make pizza with it instead.
  • Banneton: ceramic bowls lined with linen dish towels work fine. High-hydration dough sticks to cloth, so scrub rice flour into the weave, leave extra in the bottom, and sprinkle more around the sides once the loaf is in. If it sticks anyway, work a sharp knife under the stuck spot and add rice flour. For bad sticks, cut the dough free and press it back into shape before baking, carefully if the pot is already hot.
  • Storage: a bread box, or the Dutch oven with the lid cocked open; airtight containers and plastic bags kill the crust. Once cut, set the loaf cut side down; it keeps well at least three days. It freezes very well: cool completely, double wrap tightly in plastic, freeze, and thaw at room temperature, wrapped or not, before slicing.
  • Bread pans: works in two oiled 9 x 4 pans. After the final shape, form sausage-shaped loaves, set them seam side down in the pans, and continue with the cold rise as written. They may bake faster, so watch them and use the thump test.
  • Not a sandwich-bread recipe: at roughly 78% hydration counting the starter, the dough is built for an open, irregular crumb. In a Pullman pan it bakes into a rectangular artisan loaf with tunnels, and never degassing is the opposite of what sandwich crumb needs. Sandwich bread is a separate formula: bread flour, about 65% hydration, butter and honey, and deliberate degassing at shaping.
  • Half batch (1 loaf): 263 g water, 100 g starter, 350 g flour, 10 g salt; `shop` gives the same at 12 servings.
  • Per slice (24 slices), from the recipe file: 110 cal, 0 g fat, 23 g carbohydrate, 1 g fiber, 3 g protein, 332 mg sodium.
  • Revision history (November 2026; the full changelog and reasoning are in the original file): the burnt-bottom fixes were folded into the bake steps instead of sitting below the recipe and contradicting it; a cool-base, hot-lid method with a shorter bake was tried and failed (poor rise, doughy center) and was reverted to a full preheat; the preheat became 45 minutes minimum; the preheat stays at 450 F, not 500 F (Ryan's call, matching the original recipe); the covered bake went back to 30 minutes; the uncovered finish settled at 15 minutes at 475 F, as a checkpoint; doneness became an internal temperature of 208 to 210 F; and the Day 1 start moved to 4:45 pm so the dough reaches the fridge by 9:00 pm without trimming the autolyse or the bulk rise.
  • Open question carried forward: the original recipe's stretch-and-fold section says four sets over 2.5 hours, but its own header says 2 hours. This card assumes four sets at 30-minute intervals (1.5 hours of folding); if the actual practice runs longer, the Day 1 clock times shift.

recipes.title: Sourdough Cinnamon Rolls
recipes.time: about 15 hr, mostly an overnight rise
recipes.source: The Clever Carrot (Emilie Raffa)
recipes.description: A sourdough sweet dough mixed in the evening, risen overnight, and rolled, filled, and baked in the morning, finished with a cream cheese glaze.

ingredients.text: 100 g sourdough starter, bubbly and active
Cooking spray or oil, for coating
6 Tbsp unsalted butter (84 g), softened, not melted
ingredients.item: unsalted butter (84 g), softened, not melted

ingredients.text: 2/3 cup whipped cream cheese, room temperature

recipes.steps_html:
Evening (about 7 pm): the dough

  1. Combine the melted butter and milk in a small bowl and let it cool slightly. Too hot, and the dough turns sticky like cake batter; if that happens, let the dough cool before adding any more flour.
  2. In a stand mixer with the paddle, mix the egg, starter, and sugar. With the machine running, slowly pour in the milk mixture, then add the flour and salt. Mix to a rough, sticky dough, about 1 minute. Scrape down the bowl, cover with a damp towel, and rest 30 minutes.
  3. Switch to the dough hook and knead on medium-low (speed 2 or 3) for 6 to 8 minutes, until the dough is soft and supple and pulls away from the sides. Add a little flour if it is too sticky.
  4. Bulk rise: move the dough to a buttered medium bowl, cover with plastic wrap, and let it rise overnight until doubled, about 8 to 12 hours or more at 67 to 68 F.
  5. Optional: 30 minutes to 1 hour into the rise, stretch and fold. Pull a portion of dough up, fold it to the center, give the bowl a quarter turn, and repeat for 4 folds in all.

Morning: roll, fill, and shape

  1. Line a 9-inch springform pan with parchment (scrunch it into a ball first, then open it out), with enough overhang to lift the rolls out.
  2. Lightly oil and flour the counter. Turn out the dough, pat it into a rough rectangle, and rest 10 minutes.
  3. Flour the dough and the rolling pin and roll to about 16 x 12 inches, measuring. If the dough resists, rest it 5 to 10 minutes and try again.
  4. Filling: mix the softened butter with the sugar, cinnamon, and flour, and spread it over the dough with an offset spatula, leaving a 1/2-inch border.
  5. Starting on a long (16-inch) side, roll the dough into a tight log, pressing gently as you go, so the swirls hold; end seam side down. If the dough gets sticky, oil or flour your fingertips.
  6. Mark the log into equal pieces, then cut it into 2-inch sections with an oiled knife or bench scraper.
  7. Second rise: set the rolls in the lined pan and rest 1 to 2 hours, until puffy. To chill or freeze them instead, see Notes.

Bake and glaze

  1. Heat the oven to 350 F. Bake on the center rack about 30 minutes, until the tops are light golden brown.
  2. Cool in the pan 15 minutes so the butter soaks back into the dough, then lift the rolls out on the parchment to a wire rack.
  3. Glaze, while the rolls bake or cool: beat the softened butter, whipped cream cheese, and powdered sugar in a stand mixer until smooth, thinning with milk as needed. Everything should be soft and at room temperature.
  4. Top with glaze, or dust lightly with powdered sugar. Best slightly warm, the same day.
recipes.notes_html:
• Bake time (Ryan, 2022): 40 minutes, per the original recipe, came out way overdone and dry with a burned bottom; bake about 30. Ryan's note also asks whether to take the rolls out of the metal pan sooner to keep the bottom from burning (open).
  • Ryan's 150% batch, as written in the note: dough 240 g milk, 12 Tbsp butter, 1 1/2 large eggs (beat two eggs and keep about half, or use 1 egg plus 1 yolk), 150 g starter, 36 g sugar, 540 g flour, 7.5 g salt; filling 9 Tbsp butter, 150 g (3/4 cup) sugar, 4 1/2 tsp cinnamon, 1 1/2 Tbsp flour. `shop` at 12 servings gives the same amounts, with the eggs rounded up to 2. The note gives no glaze amounts, pan, or rectangle size for the bigger batch (open).
  • Serves estimate: the 16-inch log cut every 2 inches makes 8 rolls, at 1 per person.
  • Time: about 1 hour in the evening, an 8 to 12 hour rise, and about 3 1/2 hours in the morning (rolling, the 1 to 2 hour second rise, the bake, and cooling); the total is an estimate.
  • Butter in all: 18 Tbsp (2 1/4 sticks): 8 melted for the dough, 6 softened for the filling, 4 softened for the glaze.
  • Chill option: after the rolls rest 1 hour, cover and refrigerate until ready, then rest at room temperature before baking. They should be plump and puffy when they go in.
  • Make-ahead (freeze): put the cut, shaped rolls in the parchment-lined springform pan, cover with two layers of plastic wrap, and freeze. The night before baking, swap in fresh wrap (it keeps condensation from dripping onto the rolls) and thaw overnight, 10 to 12 hours at about 67 F. Bake the next morning as written.
  • Filling: the note keeps the softened-butter filling, which the source calls a variation.

recipes.title: Sourdough Crumpets (Samantha cakes)
recipes.source: King Arthur Flour
recipes.description: Unfed sourdough discard turned into four griddle crumpets in about 15 minutes, with baking soda for the rise and the holes.

ingredients.text: 1 cup sourdough starter, unfed or discard (227 g per cup)
ingredients.item: sourdough starter, unfed or discard (227 g per cup)

ingredients.text: Cooking oil and butter, for the griddle

recipes.steps_html:
1. Put the starter in a medium bowl. Stir in the sugar and salt, then the baking soda. The batter should rise, bubble a bit, and turn almost billowy.
  2. Heat a griddle over medium-low, about 300 F. Lightly oil it (skip the oil if it is nonstick) and melt a pat of butter on top.
  3. Lightly grease four English muffin rings (1 inch high, 4 inches across) and set them on the griddle. Divide the batter among them, a generous 1/4 cup each; a heaped muffin scoop does it well.
  4. Cook about 5 minutes, until the tops are set and full of small holes.
  5. Flip, lift off the rings (they should pop right off), and cook about 3 minutes more, until golden on the bottom.
  6. Serve warm, split, with butter and jam, or toast them first to brown and crisp.
recipes.notes_html:
• Also called Samantha cakes (the note's name for them).
  • Serves estimate: 4 crumpets at 2 per person.
  • Time: about 8 minutes on the griddle per the steps, plus mixing and heating the griddle; the 15 minutes is an estimate.
  • Baking soda: if the discard is particularly sour, increase it to 1/2 tsp (source's tip).
  • The note's numbers in parentheses (283 g starter, 1.25 tsp sugar, 1/2 tsp salt, .5 tsp baking soda) work out to about 1 1/4 times the recipe, as if for a 283 g batch of discard. That reading is inferred from the numbers, not written in the note.
  • Oil and butter for the griddle and butter and jam for serving are named only in the source's steps; they are added to the list here.
  • Leftovers keep at room temperature for several days; freeze, well wrapped, for longer.

recipes.title: Sourdough Discard Crackers
recipes.source: Not named in the note; its links go to bonappetit.com, so probably a Bon Appetit article (unconfirmed)
recipes.description: Discard, flour, and olive oil rolled paper-thin, baked as three giant sheet-pan crackers, and snapped into jagged pieces.

ingredients.text: 1 cup (227 g) sourdough starter discard, about
1/4 cup olive oil, about, plus more for brushing
ingredients.item: olive oil, about, plus more for brushing
ingredients.item_scaled: olive oil, about, plus more for brushing

ingredients.text: Flaky salt or other toppings, optional (see Notes)

recipes.steps_html:
1. Heat the oven to 350 F.
  2. In a medium bowl, whisk the salt and flour together with your fingers. Pour in the discard and olive oil and mix until the dough comes together; it starts shaggy and gets tauter as you go.
  3. Knead a couple of times into a smooth ball, then divide into thirds.
  4. On a sheet of parchment, roll one ball out as big and thin as you can without tearing it.
  5. Move the parchment to a sheet pan, brush the dough with a little more olive oil, and add any topping. With more pans, make all three sheets at once; otherwise bake in shifts.
  6. Bake 15 to 20 minutes, until the giant cracker is golden brown.
  7. Cool completely, then snap into jagged pieces. Store airtight at room temperature.
recipes.notes_html:
• Flour: the source likes a mix of whole wheat and all-purpose, but any flour works, including half chickpea or buckwheat flour.
  • Toppings: flaky salt is the default. Za'atar, sumac, garlic powder, or nutritional yeast also work. For heavier seasonings (fennel, cumin, poppy, or sesame seeds, dried herbs), brush with beaten egg white instead of oil, scatter the topping and press it in gently, or knead it into the dough before rolling. Sweet: cinnamon sugar, or nutritional yeast with turbinado sugar.
  • Serves estimate: about 12 oz of crackers from the batch at about 1 1/2 oz per person as a snack. This is a rough estimate; the source gives no yield.
  • Time: about 15 minutes to mix and roll plus a 20-minute bake with all three sheets in at once; baking in shifts adds about 40 minutes.
  • Source: the note names no source or author. Its links go to bonappetit.com, which points to a Bon Appetit article; a web search on 2026-11-22 did not confirm it.

recipes.title: Sourdough Discard Waffles
recipes.source: Emilie Raffa, The Clever Carrot (from her book Artisan Sourdough Made Simple); Ryan's by-weight version
recipes.description: Cinnamon-sugar waffles made with sourdough discard, by weight. One bowl, about 30 minutes start to finish.

ingredients.text: 247 g whole milk (1 cup), plus a splash more to thin
ingredients.item: whole milk (1 cup), plus a splash more to thin
ingredients.item_scaled: whole milk , plus a splash more to thin

ingredients.text: 28 g unsalted butter (2 Tbsp), melted, into the batter
ingredients.item: unsalted butter (2 Tbsp), melted, into the batter
ingredients.item_scaled: unsalted butter , melted, into the batter

ingredients.text: 14 g unsalted butter (1 Tbsp), melted, for brushing
ingredients.item: unsalted butter (1 Tbsp), melted, for brushing

recipes.steps_html:
1. Stir the sugar and cinnamon for the cinnamon sugar together in a shallow bowl.
  2. Preheat the waffle iron fully.
  3. In a large bowl, whisk the discard, milk, the melted butter for the batter, and the egg.
  4. Add the flour, the batter sugar, baking powder, and salt. Whisk until smooth. Too thick to pour? Add milk a splash at a time. A stiffer starter needs more.
  5. Spray the iron. Add about 1/2 cup plus a few spoonfuls of batter. Overfilling steams the waffle and makes it doughy.
  6. Cook 3 to 5 minutes, until golden and crisp.
  7. Move to a cutting board and brush lightly with the reserved butter.
  8. Press both sides into the cinnamon sugar.
  9. Repeat with the remaining batter, spraying the iron before every waffle. Serve with fruit, coconut, and maple syrup.
recipes.notes_html:
• Serves estimate: 4 waffles at 2 per person (the count varies with the iron). At the default 3 servings, `shop` gives the 1.5x batch (6 waffles) from the original doc; 4 servings gives its 2x batch (8 waffles).
  • The 1.5x batch in the doc uses 1 large egg plus about 25 g of a second, beaten; the shopping list rounds that up to 2 eggs.
  • Butter: 14 g per Tbsp. Melt all of it at once, then split it between the batter and brushing; keep the brushing butter for brushing only.
  • Conversions used: whole milk at 1.03 g/ml (1 cup = 247 g), fine sea salt about 6 g per tsp (an estimate; brands vary), a large egg about 50 g out of the shell.
  • Starter: written for a 100% hydration starter (equal flour and water by weight). A stiffer starter needs more milk.
  • Discard freshness: recently fed discard that smells fresh, not sour, gives the best flavor.
  • Baking powder: don't skip it. It offsets the starter's acidity and drives the rise.
  • Sticking: a fully preheated, sprayed iron keeps the waffles intact.
  • Overnight (untested): the source says resting the batter overnight deepens the flavor but gives no specifics. Mix the batter the night before and refrigerate it covered, since it holds egg and milk. Open question: whether baking powder loses lift overnight and should go in the morning instead.
  • Freezing: cool the waffles, freeze them flat on a parchment-lined sheet pan, then bag them. They keep about 2 months. Reheat in the toaster until crisp. The source suggests a double or triple batch for this.
  • Dairy-free swap: plant milk, with olive oil or vegan butter in place of butter.
  • Test log: nothing logged yet (the doc's log is empty). Record tests here: date, batch size, change, result.

recipes.title: Sourdough Pancakes
recipes.time: about 1 hr plus an overnight rest
recipes.source: NYT Cooking Instagram post; Cast-Iron Sourdough Pancake from Vinegar Hill House, adapted by Tejal Rao
recipes.description: An overnight sourdough batter baked over a thin layer of fruit in a hot cast-iron skillet, then flipped out fruit side up.

ingredients.text: 1/2 to 1 cup sourdough starter (227 g per cup)
1 Tbsp butter, plus more for serving
3 to 4 pears or apples, peeled and sliced (or sliced peaches or strawberries, or whole blueberries)
ingredients.item: pears or apples, peeled and sliced (or sliced peaches or strawberries, or whole blueberries)
ingredients.item_scaled: pears or apples, peeled and sliced (or sliced peaches or strawberries, or whole blueberries)

recipes.steps_html:
1. The night before, mix the starter, flour, and milk. Cover with a cloth and leave at room temperature overnight, up to 24 hours.
  2. Stir well. Move a scant cup of the mixture to a lidded jar and refrigerate it as starter for the next batch.
  3. Whisk the eggs, baking soda, salt, and sugar into the rest. It loosens to a thick, airy batter like a milkshake; add a splash of milk if it is too stiff.
  4. Heat the oven to 450 F with a cast-iron skillet inside (8-inch for a large pancake to cut and share, 4-inch for individual ones).
  5. Take out the hot pan, swirl in 1 Tbsp butter until melted, and add a thin layer of fruit, leaving some of the pan bottom showing.
  6. Firm fruit (apples, pears): set the pan over medium heat for 1 to 2 minutes, until the fruit softens at the edges. Soft fruit or berries: go straight to the batter.
  7. Pour in enough batter to cover the fruit completely, about 1/2 inch thick.
  8. Bake 15 minutes, until the top is evenly browned and the edges are crisp.
  9. Flip onto a plate fruit side up and serve hot with more butter and maple syrup. Repeat with the rest of the batter.
recipes.notes_html:
• Serves estimate: after the scant cup is held back, about 3 1/2 cups of batter, enough for about two 8-inch pancakes 1/2 inch thick (or about eight 4-inch ones), at half an 8-inch pancake per person.
  • Time: the steps give an overnight rest (up to 24 hours) and 15 minutes per bake; the hour covers the preheat and two 8-inch bakes and is an estimate.
  • Butter: the list gives 1 Tbsp, but each pan load takes 1 Tbsp. Plan on 2 Tbsp for two 8-inch pancakes, plus butter for serving.
  • Fruit: the source's "3 to 4" fits whole pears, apples, or peaches. It gives no amount for strawberries or blueberries; use enough for a thin layer with the pan showing through.
  • Maple syrup is named only in the serving step of the source; it is added to the list here.
  • The scant cup held back in step 2 is the next batch's starter and stays the same at any scale, so a scaled-down batch makes proportionally less batter.
  • Gram weights are as written in the note; they are for this card's amounts, and the shopping list leaves them off when it scales.

recipes.description: A soft, fine-crumbed sourdough pain de mie enriched with milk, butter, and honey, made with Ryan's own active starter and baked lidded in two Pullman pans for square slices.

ingredients.text: 149 g active sourdough starter, 100% hydration, at its peak (a spoonful floats in water)
ingredients.item: active sourdough starter, 100% hydration, at its peak (a spoonful floats in water)
ingredients.item_scaled: active sourdough starter, 100% hydration, at its peak (a spoonful floats in water)

ingredients.text: 764 g all-purpose flour (medium protein, such as King Arthur)
ingredients.item: all-purpose flour (medium protein, such as King Arthur)

ingredients.shop_item: all-purpose flour (medium protein, such as King Arthur)

ingredients.text: 305 g water, warmed or cooled so the dough lands near 78 F
ingredients.item: water, warmed or cooled so the dough lands near 78 F
ingredients.item_scaled: water, warmed or cooled so the dough lands near 78 F

ingredients.text: 100 g unsalted butter, room temperature, cut into 1/2-inch pats
ingredients.item: unsalted butter, room temperature, cut into 1/2-inch pats
ingredients.item_scaled: unsalted butter, room temperature, cut into 1/2-inch pats

recipes.steps_html:
Starter (fed to peak at mix time)

  1. Feed your starter 1:1:1 the way you usually do, timed so it peaks when you are ready to mix (often 4 to 6 hours somewhere warm). Make at least 175 g so 149 g comes out of the jar easily (60 g each of starter, flour, and water makes 180 g). Mix only when it is domed, bubbly, and a spoonful floats; if it is not there yet, wait for it.

Mix (about 45 minutes)

  1. Autolyse: in the stand mixer bowl, mix the flour, the milk, the 305 g water, and the 149 g of starter on low until just combined. Cover and rest 30 minutes.
  2. Add the honey, salt, and 25 g water on top. Mix on low until absorbed, then on medium about 6 minutes, until the dough is shaggy and clings to the hook, then on low 2 to 4 minutes more.
  3. With the mixer running, add the butter one pat at a time, letting each disappear before the next, 5 to 8 minutes in all.

Bulk (about 4 hours, by the rise, not the clock)

  1. Cover and ferment at 74 to 76 F. A kitchen even a few degrees cooler (Ryan's ran 71 to 73 F in November) stretches every stage, so use the oven with only the light on, and check it with a thermometer, since the light can push it past 80 F. A straight-sided container with the starting level marked makes the rise easy to read. Starting 30 minutes in, give the dough three sets of stretch and folds 30 minutes apart, then leave it alone. It is ready when smooth, puffy, and up about 40%, with bubbles on top and domed edges; if not, check again every 15 minutes, however long that takes.

Shape and proof (about 3 1/2 hours, by the rim, not the clock)

  1. Divide into two pieces of about 800 g. Preshape each into a round and rest uncovered 30 minutes.
  2. Oil the pans and the inside of the lids. Fold the sides of each round in, roll it into a tight cylinder, and set it seam side down in a pan. Cover the pans (a large plastic bag works).
  3. Proof at 74 to 76 F until the dough rises almost to the rim: about 2 3/4 to 3 hours at that temperature, longer in a cool kitchen. Toward the end, heat the oven with a rack in the bottom third (take the pans out first if they are proofing in it).

Bake and cool (about 1 hour, then 1 to 2 hours cooling)

  1. Slide the lids on. Bake 15 minutes at 425 F, then turn the oven to 350 F and bake 30 to 35 minutes more, to about 204 F inside. If it is under, put the pans back for 5 minutes and check again.
  2. Take the lids off, rest the loaves in the pans 10 minutes, then turn them out onto a rack. Cool completely, 1 to 2 hours, before slicing.
recipes.notes_html:
• Starter (changed 2026-11-24, Ryan's call): the source builds an overnight levain, 7 g of starter with 71 g each of flour and water (about 1:10:10), left 10 to 12 hours at 74 to 76 F, with all 149 g going into the dough. On the first bake (2026-11-24, kitchen about 71 to 73 F) that levain was much less active than Ryan's starter usually is, and after the written proof time the dough had reached only 1/3 to 1/2 of the pans. The card now starts from his own active starter: the same 149 g, and since his starter is 100% hydration like the levain, the flour and water are unchanged. The source's levain is fed plain white flour, which keeps the loaf mild; a starter fed other flours may make it a little tangier. The levain version of this card is in `_Archive/2026-11-24_sandwich-bread-levain/`.
  • More starter: at Ryan's usual 200 g (his everyday loaf's amount), the dough ferments faster and tastes a little more sour, which helps in a cool kitchen. The extra 51 g adds about 25 g each of flour and water, too little to change the dough. Go by the 40% rise, not the 4-hour clock.
  • Schedule: the step times assume 74 to 76 F. A same-day bake: feed the starter about 6:30 am, mix about 11, shape about 4 pm, bake about 7:30 pm, and slice around 10 pm. To keep the bake out of the evening, shape in the afternoon and put the covered pans in the fridge overnight (a slightly sourer loaf); in the morning, finish the proof somewhere warm until the dough is almost at the rim, then bake as written. The source gives no change to the bake for the overnight rest.
  • Proof check: by a rough estimate from the pan volume, 800 g of shaped dough starts about a third of the way up these pans, so "almost to the rim" means it has well over doubled. Dough still near that starting level after 3 hours is fermenting slowly; give it warmth and time rather than baking it.
  • Pans: two lidded Kitessensu Pullman pans (a 2-pack), 8.3 x 4.8 x 4.5 inches outside. Ryan measured the inside 2026-11-23: 7.5 x 4 inches at the bottom, 8 x 4.5 inches at the top, 4 3/8 inches high. With the sloped sides that is about 144 cubic inches.
  • Scaling: none. The source bakes two 800 g loaves in 9 x 4 x 4 inch Pullmans (144 cubic inches, nominal), and its pan chart gives 800 to 900 g for that pan. These pans hold the same, so every amount is the source's as written. A first version of this card scaled to 740 g per pan from a store listing that gave only the bottom size; it is in `_Archive/2026-11-23_sandwich-bread-740g/`.
  • Fill: other lidded Pullman recipes checked put the fill anywhere from about 4.4 to 7.1 g of dough per cubic inch, and 800 g is about 5.6. The first bake did not test it, since the dough never finished proofing. After a full proof: rounded top corners mean too little dough (go up about 50 g per pan next time; the source's chart tops out at 900 g). Dough pushing out under the lid, or a dense, tight crumb, means too much (go down).
  • Lid: the source bakes lid on the whole time for a light golden, thin crust. For a browner top, King Arthur's Pullman guidance is to take the lid off for the last 15 minutes. With no lid at all, brush with an egg wash (1 egg whisked with 1 tsp milk) and let the dough crest about 1 inch above the rim before baking.
  • Scoring: none. With the lid on, the dough rises into the lid and bakes flat against it, so a cut has no room to open and only leaves a line on top; the source has no scoring step. With no lid (the egg-wash version), a score is optional: one shallow cut down the length steers where the loaf opens, and many open-top loaves go in unscored. A split top on any version points to underproofing (Troubleshooting below), which a score does not fix.
  • Internal temperature: the source gives about 204 F on its recipe card, about 200 F in the text, and about 205 F for a loaf baked without the lid.
  • Troubleshooting, from the source's FAQ: an erratic rise or a split top means underproofed dough, so give the bulk and proof more time. Caved-in sides: leave out 20 g of the water or milk, cool 5 to 10 minutes in the pan before turning out, and bake 5 to 10 minutes longer. Grease well; a thin plastic spatula frees stuck sides.
  • Sugar for honey: start at 5% of the flour (about 42 g here) and adjust; too much sugar slows fermentation.
  • Flour: the source uses all-purpose (King Arthur, 11.7% protein) and no whole grain for the lightest crumb, and does not test bread flour. Bread flour works. Expect a sturdier, slightly chewier slice with a little more rise and a little less cottony softness, and a stiffer dough. If it feels tight, add about 10 to 20 g more water with the 25 g mix water; that amount is an untested estimate. Half bread flour, half all-purpose is a middle ground. Ryan's Sourdough Bread notes point to bread flour for sandwich loaves.
  • One change at a time: the next bake changes only the starter, and with a full proof it is also the first real test of whether 800 g fills the pans. Swap the flour on a later bake, so each result has one cause.
  • Serves estimate: about 14 half-inch slices per loaf (7 1/2 to 8 inches long), heels not counted, at 1 slice per serving.
  • Why this recipe (researched 2026-11-23): it is the only well-documented starter-only recipe written for two lidded Pullmans, with a pan chart for sizing. Its own rating base is small (5 stars from 5 reviews, over 700 comments). Other well-reviewed options, none written for a lidded pan of this size: The Clever Carrot, Easy Sourdough Sandwich Bread (4.9 from 687 reviews; one 8 1/2 x 4 loaf, butter and sugar, overnight bulk); Little Spoon Farm, Soft Sourdough Sandwich Bread (4.93 from 187 votes; the author uses a Pullman); Farmhouse on Boone, Sourdough Pain de Mie (4.78 from 45 votes; one large lidded Pullman).

recipes.steps_html:
1. Heat the oven to 425 F. Whisk or blend the yogurt with half the feta until smooth.

recipes.title: Steak Salad with Arugula and Blue Cheese

recipes.description: Seared or grilled skirt or flank steak sliced over arugula with radishes, blue cheese, and a steakhouse mustard vinaigrette.
